def test_cli_collection_subtypes(annotation, cli_args, expected):
    class Variadic(BaseSettings):
        values: CliVariadicArg[annotation]  # type: ignore[valid-type]

    class Positional(BaseSettings):
        values: CliPositionalArg[CliVariadicArg[annotation]]  # type: ignore[valid-type]

    class Plain(BaseSettings):
        values: annotation  # type: ignore[valid-type]

    for cls, args in (
        (Variadic, ['--values', *cli_args]),
        (Positional, cli_args),
        (Plain, [arg for val in cli_args for arg in ('--values', val)]),
    ):
        values = CliApp.run(cls, cli_args=args).values
        assert values == expected
        assert type(values) is type(expected)

    assert CliApp.run(Plain, cli_args=['--values', cli_args[0]]).values == type(expected)(
        [next(iter(expected.items()))] if isinstance(expected, dict) else [cli_args[0]]
    )

(`tuple[str, ...]`), bare (`tuple`) or optional (`tuple[str, ...] | None`). The parsed value has the type of the field,
e.g. `--field a --field b` results in `('a', 'b')` for a `tuple[str, ...]` field. `str`, `bytes` and `bytearray` are
not treated as collections and always take a single value.
